title: Cabin Window Frame Lower Flange — Corrosion Repair at the Reveal Drain

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Window Frame Structure

abstract: Interim repair for corrosion of the cabin window frame lower flange where condensate has collected at the reveal, including the frame variant identification that determines the repair envelope.

sections.purpose: To give the interim repair for corrosion found on the cabin window frame lower flange at the reveal drain position, and to define the limits beyond which the frame must be replaced.
sections.damage_assessment: Corrosion at the frame lower flange is caused by condensate collecting at the reveal instead of draining. It presents first as staining on the sidewall panel behind the reveal and only later as visible product on the flange. Three frame variants are in service and the flange section is not the same on all three, so the variant must be identified from the marking on the flange before the repair envelope is chosen; using the wrong envelope will either reject a repairable frame or accept one that is not. Assess the damage after removing the reveal and flushing the drain path. Record whether the path was clear, because a blocked path means the damage will return whatever the repair does. Measure the depth of the deepest pit after a light clean-up.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the pane and the reveal under the removal task and record the frame variant. Flush the drain path and record whether it was clear. Where the path is blocked, clear it mechanically with the flush kit and never with compressed air. Remove the paint and the protective finish over the affected flange length and for 40 mm beyond. Clean the area and examine it under magnification. Remove the corrosion product with a non-metallic abrasive, working along the flange, and blend the pits to a 20 to 1 ratio. Measure the remaining flange thickness at three points and compare with the limits for the identified variant. Where the loss is inside the limits, apply the two-stage surface treatment within the application window and install the cleat sub-assembly D5620124075497 if it has been removed. Where the loss exceeds the limits, the frame D5620128912144 must be replaced, which is a heavy repair outside the scope of this scheme. Install the edging grommet AGS159290-6D at the drain tube pass-through and secure the tube. Apply the sealant fillet at the flange to reveal interface and check the drain path with clean water before the reveal is installed.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of the repaired flange at every second cabin check for the first four years and thereafter at every heavy check. Flush and confirm the drain path at every inspection; a blocked path at a repaired frame requires the repair to be re-assessed rather than simply cleared. This is an interim repair and the affected window must be brought to the common frame standard at the next cabin refresh.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Flange thickness loss up to 10 per cent of nominal for the first frame variant, 8 per cent for the second and third, over a length not exceeding 120 mm, with no pit deeper than 0.4 mm after blend and no damage within 15 mm of the drain tube pass-through.

repair_drawings.title: Blend envelope and drain tube reinstatement, cabin window frame lower flange

materials.description: CLEAT, WINDOW FRAME STRUCTURE, SUB-ASSY, RH

type_data.fastener_pattern: Existing cleat pattern retained, 8 blind rivets at 25 mm pitch. No new holes are permitted in the flange within the repair envelope.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Interim repair valid for 8 000 flight cycles or until the next cabin refresh, whichever occurs first. The affected window must then be brought to the common frame standard.
